judgments.rationale: This is a pill link 'Geral' in the visible row of section links under the header (href /geral). Its text is the name of the newspaper's 'Geral' (general news) section, and on a news site's section menu that is enough to tell the purpose: it opens the Geral section. The destination, fetched live, is the section page with title 'Geral' and h2 'Geral'. So the link text alone meets 2.4.4 and there is no failure Rampa missed. One link reading 'Geral' and another link to the same address in the drawer menu point to the same place, so they are not ambiguous. The live HTML from my own fetch has the same anchor and markup as the snapshot, and the screenshot shows the styled pill row, so the capture matches what users get.
